---
title: Series
description: "One multichannel run of ordered numeric steps per record, as context or a forecast target."
---

The daily spend of an account is a run of numbers whose order matters: a payment
model can use the last 90 days as context, or forecast the next seven. `Series`
holds one such run per record. Each step carries `channels` numeric values, such
as daily amount spent and daily transaction count. Steps are ordered, not
timestamped; use a [Branch](branch.qmd) with [Period](dateparts.qmd) when the
calendar position of each item matters.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    recent=rf.Series(channels=2, length=90, overflow="tail"),
    next_week=rf.Series(channels=2, horizon=7, mask=True),
)
```

One record:

```yaml
recent:
  - [84.50, 3]
  - [0.00, 0]
  - [12.20, 1]
next_week:
  - [40.00, 2]
  - [0.00, 0]
```

The record shows three days of history and two forecast days; real records carry
the full `length` and `horizon`. Every step in the history is known at the
decision time. Use [Number](number.qmd) for a single value per record and
[Branch](branch.qmd) when each step has fields of different types.

## Input and options

Each valued input takes one of four Arrow shapes. Each row below shows the same
three steps of temperature and humidity:

| Shape | Arrow type per record | Example record | Field |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| list | `list<number>` | `[21.5, 22.0, 22.4]` | `rf.Series(channels=1)` |
| list of lists | `list<list<number>>` or `list<fixed_size_list<number, C>>` | `[[21.5, 0.61], [22.0, 0.58], [22.4, 0.55]]` | `rf.Series(channels=2)` |
| list of structs | `list<struct<temp: number, hum: number>>` | `[{temp: 21.5, hum: 0.61}, {temp: 22.0, hum: 0.58}, {temp: 22.4, hum: 0.55}]` | `rf.Series(channels=("temp", "hum"))` |
| struct of lists | `struct<temp: list<number>, hum: list<number>>` | `{temp: [21.5, 22.0, 22.4], hum: [0.61, 0.58, 0.55]}` | `rf.Series(channels=("temp", "hum"))` |

Large lists and fixed-size lists are accepted wherever lists are: for the outer
list of a list of structs and for the channel lists of a struct of lists. Values convert to `float64`; integers beyond ±2^53 are rejected.

The two struct shapes accept either form of `channels`:

- A tuple of names selects those struct members, in tuple order. Other members
  are ignored, so `channels=("hum",)` reads only humidity and
  `channels=("hum", "temp")` swaps the channel order. A named member that is
  absent raises an error.
- An integer reads every member, in struct order, and must equal the member
  count. `channels=2` reads both examples above; `channels=3` raises an error.

Every struct member must be numeric (list of structs) or a list of numbers
(struct of lists). A struct with a string member or with mixed members is
rejected when relflow checks the input Arrow types, even when `channels` does
not name that member; narrow it in a [preprocessor](#reshaping-in-a-preprocessor). A tuple of
names on a list or list of lists raises an error, because those shapes have no
member names.

### Missing values

A step is observed only when every one of its channels is finite. A null, NaN,
or infinite value makes its step unobserved, silently: the rest of the series
stays valid, and the encoder sees which steps were observed. This covers a null
value inside a list, a null step in a list of lists, and a null step struct or
null member value in a list of structs.

A null channel list in a struct of lists is a missing channel, not a missing
step, so it is never silent. relflow emits a `UserWarning` that names the field and the
channel, then reads the record. The warning shows once per field and channel
under the default Python warning filter, so it does not count records:

- When some channel lists are null, those channels are NaN at every step of the
  record, so its steps are unobserved.
- When every named channel list is null, the series is empty.

In one record, every non-null channel list must hold the same number of steps.
Lists of different lengths raise an error naming the field, the channels, and
the first record that differs.

An empty series is `valued`. A non-empty series with no observed step takes the
`other` [value state](index.qmd#value-state). A null series is `null`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channels` | required | Positive number of values per step, or a tuple of struct member names. A tuple sets the count and order, selects those members, and requires struct input. An integer needs exactly that many struct members. |
| `length` | `None` | Hard cap on retained steps. `None` keeps the whole series and pads each batch to its longest. |
| `overflow` | `None` | With a finite `length`: `head` (default), `tail`, `random`, or `error`. Rejected when `length` is `None`. |
| `horizon` | `None` | Steps to predict. Required on reconstruction targets (`mask=True` or a reconstructing ancestor), rejected otherwise. |
| `n_blocks` | `6` | Number of dilated convolution blocks. |
| `jitter` | `rf.Jitter()` | Training noise on input steps. |
| `objective` | `"l2"` | Forecast loss: mean `"l1"` or `"l2"` error over predicted steps and channels. |

Overflow follows [Branch](branch.qmd): use `tail` for recency-ordered history.
With `random`, training draws a contiguous window of steps and later phases keep
the tail. A forecast target pads to exactly `horizon` steps and rejects a longer
series.

## Encoding

Per-channel statistics learned from training observations standardize the
steps. Standardized steps pass through a linear projection to the model width,
then `n_blocks` residual blocks of two dilated convolutions with dilation
doubling at each block. A masked max-pool collapses the result to one token, so
the field adds one token to its record however long the series is. Padding and
unobserved steps never contribute, and an embedding does not depend on the
padded width of the batch.

With `n_blocks=k`, each step feature sees up to `1 + 4 * (2^k - 1)` neighboring
steps: 253 at the default of six. The masked max-pool then covers every
retained observed step, so any of them can influence the token. Choose
`n_blocks` so that the local context per step matches the patterns that matter.
Apply `length` to bound memory.

## Reshaping in a preprocessor

`Series` reads one field. When the channels live elsewhere, gather them into
one of the shapes above with a [preprocessor](../guides/preprocessing.qmd). A
struct of lists is usually the shortest route, because `pl.struct` combines
list columns directly.

Channels from separate columns or nested paths become a struct of lists:

```python
import polars as pl
import relflow as rf


@rf.preprocess
def gather(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return frame.with_columns(
        signals=pl.struct(
            temp=pl.col("temp"),
            hum=pl.col("weather").struct.field("humidity"),
        ),
    )
```

Read it with `signals=rf.Series(channels=("temp", "hum"))`.

Long-format data has one row per step. Sort by step and group by record to get
one row per record with a struct of lists:

```python
@rf.preprocess
def collect(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return (
        frame.sort("step")
        .group_by("id", maintain_order=True)
        .agg(pl.col("temp"), pl.col("hum"))
        .select("id", signals=pl.struct("temp", "hum"))
    )
```

Here `frame` has the columns `id`, `step`, `temp` and `hum`. The sort by `step`
fixes the order of the steps inside each list, and `maintain_order=True` keeps
the order of the records. Without the sort, the steps follow row order. Read the
result with `signals=rf.Series(channels=("temp", "hum"))`.

A list of lists becomes a named struct of lists, one channel per position:

```python
@rf.preprocess
def name(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return frame.with_columns(
        signals=pl.struct(
            temp=pl.col("readings").list.eval(pl.element().list.get(0)),
            hum=pl.col("readings").list.eval(pl.element().list.get(1)),
        ),
    )
```

When the steps are fixed-size lists (`list<pl.Array>`), `list.get` fails on the
inner element. Use `.arr.get` instead:

```python
@rf.preprocess
def name_fixed(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return frame.with_columns(
        signals=pl.struct(
            temp=pl.col("readings").list.eval(pl.element().arr.get(0)),
            hum=pl.col("readings").list.eval(pl.element().arr.get(1)),
        ),
    )
```

Both forms give `struct<temp: list<float64>, hum: list<float64>>`.

A list of step records with a non-numeric member, such as
`[{temp: 21.5, hum: 0.61, station: "a"}, ...]`, fails the type check. Keep only
the numeric members to make a list of structs:

```python
@rf.preprocess
def narrow(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return frame.with_columns(
        hourly=pl.col("hourly").list.eval(
            pl.struct(
                pl.element().struct.field("temp"),
                pl.element().struct.field("hum"),
            ),
        ),
    )
```

Read it with `hourly=rf.Series(channels=("temp", "hum"))`.

A struct of lists with a text member, such as
`{temp: [...], hum: [...], station: "a"}`, fails the type check in the same
way. Rebuild the struct from the numeric members only:

```python
@rf.preprocess
def narrow_columns(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return frame.with_columns(
        signals=pl.struct(
            pl.col("signals").struct.field("temp"),
            pl.col("signals").struct.field("hum"),
        ),
    )
```

To avoid the null channel warning, either drop the records whose channel is
missing:

```python
@rf.preprocess
def complete(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    return frame.filter(pl.col("hum").is_not_null())
```

or fill the missing channel with nulls, one per step of another channel, so its
steps read as unobserved:

```python
@rf.preprocess
def fill(frame: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    # Multiplying by None keeps the step count of temp and makes every value null.
    unobserved = pl.col("temp").list.eval(pl.element() * None)
    return frame.with_columns(hum=pl.col("hum").fill_null(unobserved))
```

Apply either before gathering the columns into a struct.

## Learning and output

As a forecast target, `Series` predicts `horizon` steps of `channels` values
from the context of the record. The loss is the `objective` error over target steps
observed in the source, after both sides are standardized per channel.
Predictions are decoded back to source units. MAE and RMSE metrics report in
source units.

Classify a series by pairing it with a sibling target such as
`label=rf.Category(mask=True)`. `embed=True` exports a series embedding of the
model width. See [shared leaf options](index.qmd#shared-leaf-options).

In [prediction output](../reference/prediction-output.qmd), `content` is a list
of `horizon` steps. With integer `channels`, each step is a list of float64
values; with named channels, each step is a struct with one float64 member per
name, in tuple order. The writer emits
exactly `horizon` steps per coordinate. Parquet round-trips these lists,
including inside a `Branch` with null items. As with other decoded fields, read
the shared `state` and `inferred` members to learn whether a series was
reconstructed.
